knowledge-base.overview: Language-specific idioms, guardrails, and patterns for C# 12+ and .NET 8+. Loaded automatically when agents work on .cs, .csx, or .csproj files. Covers nullable reference types, async/await patterns, LINQ, records, pattern matching, dependency injection, and testing with xUnit, NSubstitute, and FluentAssertions for ASP.NET Core, console apps, and libraries.

core-principles.principle: Enable nullable reference types project-wide. Treat nullable warnings as errors. Nullability is a compile-time contract.
Prefer records, `readonly`, and `init` properties for data types. Mutable state is opt-in.
Use async/await end-to-end. Never block on async code with .Result or .Wait().
Constructor injection via IServiceCollection. No service locator pattern. No static access to dependencies.
Validate inputs at boundaries using guard clauses and ArgumentException. Never allow invalid state to propagate.

guardrail.rule: Never call .Result or .Wait() on a Task. This causes deadlocks in ASP.NET Core and Blazor. Use await end-to-end.
Always accept a CancellationToken in async methods that perform I/O. Pass it through to all downstream calls.
Never put side effects inside LINQ queries (no mutations, no I/O, no logging). LINQ is for projection and filtering only.
Enable nullable reference types in every .csproj. Never suppress nullable warnings with `#pragma warning disable` without a documented justification.
Materialize LINQ queries before returning them from a method. Never return IQueryable or deferred IEnumerable from service/repository methods — callers cannot control execution context.
guardrail.bad: public IEnumerable<User> GetActiveUsers() => _dbContext.Users.Where(u => u.IsActive); // deferred — executes outside the scope

guardrail.rule: Suffix all async method names with `Async`: GetUserAsync, SaveOrderAsync, ProcessPaymentAsync.
guardrail.good: public async Task<User> GetUserAsync(int id, CancellationToken ct = default) { ... }

guardrail.rule: Use `is not null` over `!= null` for null checks. Use `??` for defaults and `?.` for conditional access. Prefer null-coalescing over explicit null checks.
Use AsNoTracking() for all read-only EF Core queries. Tracking adds overhead and can cause stale data issues when the same DbContext processes multiple reads.
guardrail.bad: var users = await _dbContext.Users .Where(u => u.IsActive) .ToListAsync(ct); // tracked unnecessarily

guardrail.rule: Use `Any()` instead of `Count() > 0`. Count() may enumerate the entire collection; Any() short-circuits.
Use `ConfigureAwait(false)` in library code (not in ASP.NET Core controller actions). Library code must not capture the synchronization context.
guardrail.note: In ASP.NET Core apps there is no synchronization context, so ConfigureAwait(false) is not required in controller or service code there. It is required in library code targeting multiple frameworks.

guardrail.rule: Use `ValueTask<T>` for hot paths that frequently complete synchronously. Use `Task<T>` as the default; only switch to ValueTask after profiling.
Use file-scoped namespaces (`namespace MyApp.Services;`) in all new files. This reduces nesting and matches the .editorconfig warning.
Run `dotnet format` before every commit. Configure `.editorconfig` and `Directory.Build.props` at the solution root so all projects share the same style settings.

directory.purpose: ASP.NET Core host, entry point, controllers, middleware, Program.cs
Use cases, CQRS commands/queries, interfaces, application services
Entities, value objects, domain events, domain exceptions — zero external dependencies
EF Core, external services, file I/O — implements Application interfaces
Unit tests — one project per src project is fine
API + database integration tests with WebApplicationFactory
Architecture rule tests (optional, using NetArchTest or ArchUnitNET)
Shared build properties for all projects (Nullable, TreatWarningsAsErrors, analyzers)
Consistent formatting and style rules across the team

project-structure.note: Domain has zero external dependencies. Application depends only on Domain. Infrastructure depends on Application and Domain. Api is the composition root and depends on all. Test projects mirror the src/ structure.

pattern.name: Records for Immutable Data
pattern.context: DTOs, value objects, domain events, query results
pattern.description: Records provide value equality, immutability, and concise syntax. Use `with` for nondestructive mutation. Use readonly record struct for high-performance value types.

pattern.name: Guard Clauses and Nullable Contracts
pattern.context: Service and repository constructors, method boundaries
pattern.description: Validate at the entry point. Use ArgumentException static helpers (.NET 6+) for concise guards. Throw immediately — do not propagate invalid state.

pattern.name: Pattern Matching
pattern.context: Domain logic, discount rules, state transitions, type dispatch
pattern.description: Switch expressions with property, relational, and type patterns replace long if-else chains. The compiler warns if a case is missing.

pattern.name: Async Streams
pattern.context: Streaming large result sets — logs, reports, event feeds
pattern.description: IAsyncEnumerable<T> produces items lazily. Use [EnumeratorCancellation] for proper cancellation support. Consume with await foreach.

pattern.name: Dependency Injection Registration
pattern.description: Register services as extension methods on IServiceCollection. Constructor injection only — no service locator, no static access.

rules.rule: Framework: xUnit (preferred); NUnit or MSTest are acceptable but pick one per solution
Mocking: NSubstitute or Moq — pick one per project and stay consistent
Assertions: FluentAssertions for readable, descriptive assertions
Use [Theory] with [InlineData] for parameterized / data-driven tests
One assertion concept per test (multiple Should calls for the same concept are fine)
Use WebApplicationFactory for integration tests — do not spin up a real server

tool.name: dotnet list package --vulnerable
tool.purpose: Audit packages for known CVEs before adding new ones

build-config.description: Shared Directory.Build.props for all projects in the solution.
build-config.example:
<!-- Directory.Build.props --> <Project> <PropertyGroup> <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework> <Nullable>enable</Nullable> <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings> <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors> <EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>true</EnforceCodeStyleInBuild> <AnalysisLevel>latest-recommended</AnalysisLevel> </PropertyGroup>
<ItemGroup> <PackageReference Include="Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.NetAnalyzers" Version="8.0.0" PrivateAssets="all" /> <PackageReference Include="SonarAnalyzer.CSharp" Version="9.32.0" PrivateAssets="all" /> </ItemGroup> </Project>

quick-reference.item: Enable globally in Directory.Build.props; never suppress without justification
Forbidden — await end-to-end; these cause deadlocks
Required in all async I/O method signatures
All async methods must end in Async
Forbidden inside LINQ queries — project and filter only
Required for all read-only EF Core queries
Use Any() not Count() > 0 — short-circuits enumeration
Use for DTOs and value objects; with-expression for nondestructive mutation
Switch expressions with property/relational/type patterns over if-else chains
Constructor injection only; no service locator or static dependencies
Use `is not null` over `!= null`; `??` for defaults; `?.` for conditional access
Mandatory for new files — reduces nesting
xUnit + NSubstitute + FluentAssertions; WebApplicationFactory for integration tests
dotnet format before every commit; dotnet list package --vulnerable before adding deps
